title: Money math: counting, earning, saving and spending
audience: a child in grades K–5 working with an adult helper who reads along
purpose: Name coins and bills and count money, make change, compare prices, tell needs from wants, earn and set a savings goal, track spending in a simple chart, and see how a bank keeps money safe and pays a little interest.
primary_reading: Money as You Grow (Consumer Financial Protection Bureau)

weeks.4: Comparing prices: which is the better buy?
weeks.10: Interest: money that grows a little
weeks.12: Smart choices and spotting tricks in ads

blocks.deliverable: Count three handfuls of coins and write each total.
Play store: buy three items and make change.
Sort ten pictures into needs and wants and explain two choices.
Week 7 midterm; make a savings chart for a goal you choose.
Track a pretend bank balance for four weeks with interest.
Explain one ad and what it wants you to buy.
Submit the project; take an unseen 30 minute final in week 14.

project: Saving plan: choose something to save for, find its price, make a weekly plan with earning, saving and spending columns, keep the chart for four weeks (real or pretend), and present how close you came and what you would change.
completion: finish the project, take the week 7 midterm and week 14 cumulative final, then complete a new cumulative assessment after 1 to 2 weeks. Explain one major idea aloud without notes.
